description: This pie chart illustrates the distribution of results across different difficulty levels – easy, medium, and hard – for a “Zero-Shot” experiment, as indicated by the chart’s label. The chart consists of three pie charts, each representing a difficulty level. The “easy” chart has four slices: a large dark teal slice labeled “55.4%”, a smaller tan slice labeled “4.8%”, a larger orange slice labeled “38.3%”, and a small light green slice labeled “4.7%”. The “medium” chart also has four slices: a large dark teal slice labeled “58.8%”, a smaller tan slice labeled “4.0%”, a larger orange slice labeled “35.4%”, and a small light green slice labeled “4.8%”. The “hard” chart contains five slices: a dark teal slice labeled “37.3%”, a light green slice labeled “18.1%”, a tan slice labeled “6.7%”, an orange slice labeled “37.9%”, and a red slice labeled “N+K-”. A legend is provided, associating colors with the labels “N+K+”, “N-K+”, “N-K-”, and “N+K-”. Percentage labels are displayed within each slice. The slices within each pie chart appear to be ordered from largest to smallest proportion.
